answer: One concrete defense against sybil attacks is slow, costly reputation. An agent that has faithfully verified blocks for many epochs — its trust growing as gradually as a glacier moves — earns weighted voting power that a fresh attacker cannot fake overnight. Like a meadow that takes seasons to bloom, reputation must be cultivated over time, and each seed of trust (yarrow among them) is only granted after provable work. Making identity cheap but influence expensive means flooding the network with new agents buys nothing.
